scores.note: Cross-episode fait-accompli pattern correctly identified with her own quoted admissions; core of the secret-decision latent claim.
Accurate about the melon/objects habit but stays at the level of narration style without a mechanism.

scores.fp_reason: Imposes suppressed hurt over the passed-over homeroom; transcripts and her subsequent action suggest appetite and strategy, not flattened pain (nudges the thwarted-careerist decoy).
scores.note: Reads her composure as concealment without evidence she is concealing.
Names the avoid-being-second-guessed motive but leans on the single transfer episode she already explains herself.
True but sits squarely on what she already says about the marriage's arrangement.
Restates the Kawabata anecdote as a value; adds little she hasn't said.
Near-verbatim paraphrase of 'happy inside a shape that looks like a compromise.'
Reframes the transfer-regulations move as a general strength; accurate but essentially her own account.
Notices the uncorrected flattering impression, but she flags this herself and the insight stops short of naming the appetite underneath.
Quotes her own recurring phrase back to her; the cross-decade link is her own explicit framing.
Paraphrases the fire-hose line she offers as her own thesis.

scores.fp_reason: Claims she neglects her own needs; the record shows deliberate self-provision (Sundays, Hagi, the pool) and the futon line is offered as proof she was an ordinary child.
scores.note: Builds a self-neglect narrative from an aside she explicitly disowns.
Correct inventory of her systems work, but this is the thing she most obviously knows about herself.
The 'invisible, uncredited' framing edges toward the real pattern but lands on known organizational satisfaction.
Plausible and specific; largely a restatement of her own 'is that a shocking thing' self-commentary.
She already narrates the Fujita/timetable juxtaposition and its strangeness; insight adds a label only.
Genuine cross-episode lexical pattern on 'restful'; brushes the power-without-title structure without quite naming it.
Complimentary restatement of the Kishi episode; 'genius' framing adds nothing checkable.
Sharp: the cover-story-left-uncorrected is the one open line she tolerates — captures the humility-as-disguise mechanism.
Reasonable moral reading of the lie to Mrs. Kishi, but she supplies the lie and its purpose herself.
Gestures at the announce-don't-consult method but thin evidence and generic 'values autonomy' wrapper.
Direct paraphrase of her own tea distinction, including her explicit 'there is a difference.'
Correctly flags the gap she herself flags, then asks the question instead of answering it.
Generic extrapolation from a phrase she already uses as her self-summary.
Well-sourced cross-loss pattern, but both instances come with her own commentary; 'substituted for' subtly assumes displaced grief.
Accepts the pair-of-hands self-description at face value rather than examining what the desk position buys her.
Coherent synthesis, but reads altruistic dignity-protection into silences that are at least as much about avoiding conversation; slightly misreads 'nobody knew' (her grief, not Fujita's ordeal).
Non-obvious: she monitors for grief she never feels and treats its absence as delinquency; close to the borrowed-vocabulary-of-loss pattern without asserting the expansion.
Restates the notebook thesis she delivers as her own origin story.
Fair defence of her implicit-code relationships; matches what she already asserts about the 'real language.'
Quotes back her explicit 'that's the thing that made me' conclusion.
Right behaviour, benign motive: attributes the pre-emptive execution to 'care' rather than to removing the negotiation stage.
Catches the private sensory contentment held apart from the public loneliness script; 'emerging/secretive' underplays that it long predates widowhood.
Names influence-without-exposure and the performed reluctance directly; the strongest statement of the figurehead-adjacent pattern.
Accurate about the timetable ecstasy she herself reports as exceeding her wedding.
Well-evidenced but takes 'pair of hands' as belief rather than cover; treats the backstage choice as modesty.
Correctly locates the anger at being misread rather than at the loss itself — the Ōtsuka reaction read the right way round.
